section: §2.1 FD (one G3 ρ_cr for cells 26–36), §4.1 parameters, §4.7 re-centring, §5.3 P5a-k / P2, §6.1 F1 (one shared Δ), §0.7
problem:
At c1 = c2 = 1, B1 and B2 have the same per-lane capacity: both are 2-lane G3 cells with one ρ_cr, v_f and a, and no parameter tells the two heads apart. The data say B2's merge section carries clearly more.

My read-only estimate on the cached data covered all 52 Wednesdays, validation days included, so it must be disclosed in §0.5. It used the corridor rule with Anderson Lakes speed from 5423, the longest episode ≥ 30 min, and the C4 window from onset + 2 bins to the end:
- **Merge-section flow per lane** (downstream station + exit, over 2 lanes): B1 = (Pioneer Tr + X12)/2 = 1,745 veh/h/lane (IQR 1,711–1,811; n = 28). B2 = (Old Shakopee Rd + X13)/2 = 1,950 (IQR 1,876–1,974; n = 23).
- **Same days:** on the 16 days heavy at both, B2 exceeds B1 by a median 11.4 %, and B2 is higher on 16 of 16 days.
- **Pre-onset 15-min maximum per lane:** 1,846 at B1 against 2,074 at B2.
- **Exits during discharge:** X12 ≈ 83 veh/h, X13 ≈ 204 veh/h.

With one merge-cell capacity C per lane (scaled by the same emergent drop at both heads), the model's discharge is about C − 42 at Pioneer Tr and C − 102 at Old Shakopee Rd. P5a's ±5 % then needs:
- C ≤ 1.05 × 1,704 + 42 ≈ 1,831 at B1;
- C ≥ 0.95 × 1,850 + 102 ≈ 1,860 at B2.

These ranges do not overlap. The δ_m term pushes the wrong way: E14 (≈ 480–710 veh/h in B2 discharge) depresses B2 more than E13 (≈ 145 veh/h) depresses B1. P2 is also at risk: in reality B1 breaks first because it is weaker, and an equal-capacity plant has no structural reason to do so.

The §4.7 estimator would expose the gap (m1 < 1 < m2), but re-centring c_k / m_k discards it by design. The gate plant then keeps B1 too strong and B2 too weak, and H1's two-head interaction is decided by that.

F1 is triggered by P5a but has one shared Δ on a shared ρ_cr, so it cannot change the B2/B1 ratio. The result is a route stop whose cause is foreseeable from data already inspected.
proposed_change:
Before the commit, give each head its own capacity level in the deterministic plant.
- **New parameter:** a fitted head-capacity factor θ1 on ρ_cr of the B1 head cell only (cell 26), bounds e.g. [0.75, 1.05] [lab convention]. Disclose it as geometry-motivated: the 3→2 exit-lane end at km 3.751 plus the E13 merge, a lane drop the model gives no φ. Optionally add θ2 on cell 31. Then n = 15–16, the popsize is restated, and θ1 is added to the §4.5 profiles with its seed range.
- **Capacity factors:** c_k multiplies θ_k ρ_cr,G3, so re-centring to c = 1 keeps each head at its own fitted level.
- **New fact before calibration:** add to F8 the real merge-section flow per lane at B1 and B2 (station + exit)/2, discharge and pre-onset 15-min maximum. Pre-register that the plant must reproduce their ratio (report the model's ratio next to P5a).
- **Alternative:** a φ-type lane-drop term at the X11 exit-lane end with its own coefficient. State whichever is chosen in A1 and disclose the inspection above in §0.5.

section: §4.7 (c2 on cells 31–32; consistent set C_d; re-centring unclipped), §5.3 P8/N0 only at c = 1, P6s/P10 judge only P_k status, §1.7 steps (a)/(c), §7 R3
problem:
c2 scales only cells 31–32. The cell downstream of B2 runs at c = 1: cell 33 is G3 under the base geometry and under §1.7 (a)/(c), which keep a 319-m 2-lane G3 cell from km 7.199 to 7.518. Cell 32's outflow is at most c2·C − X13, with X13 ≈ 204 veh/h in B2 discharge, about 5 % of the 2-lane flow.

So for c2 above about 1 + X13/C ≈ 1.05, the binding cell moves to cell 33, downstream of the Old Shakopee Rd station. The plant then shows a bottleneck at (Old Shakopee Rd, T.H.101), outside the controlled system; E3(ii) excludes real days with such a bottleneck. Under §1.7 (b) the same happens whenever c2·C − X13 + E15 exceeds the fitted G4 capacity. G4 is weakly identified and has no incentive to exceed the c = 1 need.

Nothing catches this:
- **C_d** checks only E_k / O_k at P_1 and P_2, so a draw with a spurious downstream head counts as "B2 inactive, consistent";
- **N0 and P8** run only at c = 1;
- **P6s and P10** score only P_k status.

Re-centring is unclipped, so draws reach 1.20 / m2 (e.g. 1.33 if m2 = 0.9), beyond the grid on which the estimator was checked. About half of all draws have c2 > 1, so the relocation regime can be frequent in the gate plant.

It also feeds the estimator: real-active B2 days that need c2 > 1.05 cannot show a P_2 episode and become "not reproducible", which pushes towards "F̂ not estimable". If the B1/B2 capacity gap (issue 1) is left in, m2 > 1 makes this more likely.
proposed_change:
Pre-register the following.
- (i) **Consistent set:** C_d also requires no model episode at any pair outside {P_1, P_2} that the real day lacks.
- (ii) **Bounded support:** compute the relocation threshold c2* per plant (the c2 at which cell 33, or G4, becomes binding on the calibration days) and bound the factor's support by it. Draws above c2* are clipped to c2* ("no B2 breakdown"), and the clipped share is reported. Also clip re-centred factors to the estimation grid range.
- (iii) **Gate the stochastic plant on numerics and spurious heads:** N0s and P8s, using the 200 draws per validation day. Example rule: the expected number of spurious-episode days ≤ the P8 limit. A FAIL gives "PASS, deterministic-only".
- (iv) **Unit test:** at c2 = c2* + 0.01, show and log the relocation.

problem:
N0 and the J penalty count only density clipping and upper-speed clipping. Activations of the v_min floor are "part of the model, reported only".

At allowed bound corners the anticipation term is very large. With ν = 90 km²/h, τ = 10 s, κ = 5 and L = 352 m, νT/(τL) ≈ 128 km/h, and at a queue tail (Δρ/(ρ + κ) ≈ 3) one step changes the speed by about 400 km/h. A parameter set whose queue tails chatter on the v_min floor every step is therefore admissible and can pass N0.

Step-halving, the only numerical-convergence check, is reported and not gated. The congestion dynamics the gate relies on (onset, extent, duration) could be numerical artefacts, and nothing would fail.
proposed_change:
Count v_min activations in cells with ρ_i < ρ_cr,i (i.e. not in a genuine jam) in the 1 % admissibility limit and in N0.

Gate step-halving at the frozen optimum: |ΔJ| / J ≤ 5 % [lab convention], and unchanged P_1 and P_2 episode days on the calibration days. A failure counts as an N0 FAIL.

section: §3.2.1 EA-1, §3.2.4 (raw speeds for events, scaled for J), §5.1 'identical to the real side', §5.2 B1 minima, §4.7 F̂_1, §9.1 'B1 measured through one lane'; D3.4 premise
problem:
EA-1 makes B1 observable by taking Anderson Lakes Pkwy speed from lane 5423 alone. The model reads a cross-section speed v_i. The corridor rule is therefore not applied to the same quantity on both sides, and B1's real activity looks largely like a lane artefact. These are my read-only reproductions on cached 2023 Wednesdays, all 52 including validation days, using the corridor estimator without the §3 exclusions:
- Raw 5423 → Pioneer Tr: P_1 is active on 27/51 days, which matches the reviewer's figure.
- With the protocol's own c_s applied to the event speed: 8/51. Here c_s = G3 interior median 70.9 / 62.5 = 1.134, from calibration-day 05–06 medians AL 62.5, PT 71.8, OSR 70.9 mph. On validation days the count drops from 13/23 to 5/23, which would trip the n_A,1 ≥ 8 minimum.
- On the 9 Wednesdays on which 5424 is alive (Nov 1 to Dec 27), 5423 alone flags B1 on 5 days and the two-lane station on 2.
- 05–06 medians on those same 9 days: 5423 63.8, 5424 80.3, both lanes 69.7, Pioneer Tr 73.3 mph. The single lane sits about 6 mph below the cross-section, so this is not just a detector fault.
Consequences:
- J fits the model to c_s-scaled Anderson Lakes speeds, while every gated B1 event uses raw single-lane speeds. The model is fitted to one target and judged against another.
- P2, P3-1, P4-1 and P7a-1 can fail on the artefact. P4-1 and P7a-1 are in the F1 trigger set, so a measurement artefact can launch the structural fallback.
- §9.1's claim that the bias 'pushes towards a false FAIL, not a false PASS' does not hold for the stochastic plant. F̂_1 is estimated to reproduce the inflated real B1 activity, and P10-1 and P6s-1 are scored against it. The gate's stochastic plant is then calibrated to too-frequent B1 breakdowns, which inflates the prize: the false-GO direction.
- Whether the B1 minima are met, which means INCONCLUSIVE or not, depends on this unregistered choice.
proposed_change:
Before the commit, add an author item (it bears on D3.4) and fix one symmetric B1 event measure:
- (a) Model-side emulation: the model's Anderson Lakes event speed is mapped to lane-1 speed by a frozen mapping estimated on calibration days with 5424 alive, disclosed as thin (n = 5); or
- (b) real-side correction with a pre-registered speed-dependent factor; or
- (c) B1 rows (P3-1, P4-1, P6-1, P7a-1, P6s-1, P10-1, and B1's part of P2 and P9) are reported only, P_1 rows are removed from the F1 trigger set, and c1 is not estimated (F̂ only for c2).
Add a pre-calibration fact, real data only: on every day with all Anderson Lakes lanes valid, the agreement of the 1-lane and all-lane P_1 day status and episode minutes. Pre-register that if the 1-lane measure flags B1 on more than a fixed share of the days the all-lane measure does not (e.g. > 25 %), option (c) applies. Delete the 'false FAIL only' sentence in §9.1, and disclose that this check used validation days.

problem:
The c_s rule is ambiguous in two ways that change the fitted target.
(1) c_s is defined only for 'interior' stations, yet S_v,d adds T.H.101 and §4.2 says real speeds are 'scaled by c_s'. It is undefined whether T.H.101 is scaled, and whether it counts in G3's reference m_G.
(2) G3's m_G is the median of only three interior stations (Anderson Lakes, Pioneer Tr, Old Shakopee Rd), one of which is the single-lane 5423 station.
My calibration-day 05–06 medians: AL 62.5, PT 71.8, OSR 70.9, T.H.101 62.7 mph.
- Interior-only m_G = 70.9 gives c_s = 1.134 (AL), 0.987 (PT) and 1.0 (OSR).
- Including T.H.101 gives m_G = 66.8 and c_s = 1.069, 0.930, 0.942 and 1.065.
Either reading is defensible, and they shift every G3 speed target in J and P1c by about 6 %. Left unscaled, T.H.101 reads about 8 mph below the rest of G3, which pulls v_f,G3 down in calibration (G4 ties v_f to G3 under §1.7 (b)). This is an unregistered forking path with a numeric effect.
proposed_change:
State explicitly:
- whether T.H.101 belongs to G3 (or G4) for m_G, and whether its speed is scaled in S_v (recommended: compute c_s for T.H.101 like the interior stations);
- that m_G is the median over stations whose speed lanes equal all their lanes, so the EA-1 single-lane station cannot set the group reference.
Put the resulting rule in unit test 10 or 14 with a toy example.

section: §5.3 P3-k, P4-k, P7a-k, P7b, P8; §5.4 P8 ('P_1 and P_2 are judged by P2–P7')
§0.3 'PASS, deterministic-only'; §5.3 stochastic rows P6s-k, P10a-k, P10b-k; §7 R3 (b)
problem:
Each stochastic row is sized for a correct plant (P6s and P10a at about 5 % each), but they form a conjunction of four sized tests: P6s-1, P6s-2, P10a-1, P10a-2. A correctly calibrated stochastic plant is then rejected about 19 % of the time (stylised, assuming independence).
On top of that, P10b-k is a point comparison with the climatology Brier score. A plant whose true skill equals climatology fails each P10b row about half the time, and §9.1 already says the benchmark 'is not easy to beat at n ≈ 20'. A PASS with F̂ is therefore improbable even for a good stochastic plant.
The fallback, 'deterministic-only', lets the gate run on the plant §0.3 calls over-predictable (the false-GO-prone one), via an author decision that is unconstrained and taken after seeing which stochastic row failed. This is a post-hoc forking path towards the biased plant.
proposed_change:
(i) Control the family-wise level across the stochastic rows. For example, size the four tests at 0.05/4: tails of 0.0032 per half in P6s, the 98.75th percentile in P10a.
(ii) Make P10b a non-inferiority test with a margin fixed now (e.g. Brier_plant ≤ Brier_clim + 0.02 [lab convention]), or report it only.
(iii) Pre-register, as a new author item before the commit, the consequence of 'deterministic-only'. For example, either no METANET gate (route to the SUMO decision), or a gate on the deterministic plant only with a stated stricter GO rule. Do not leave it to a decision taken after the stochastic results are seen.

problem:
The extension can multiply n_val by about 5 (24 Wednesdays plus up to 104 Tuesdays and Thursdays), but some n-dependent quantities are not restated for it.
- P8(i) uses an absolute tolerance ('model episode-days − real episode-days ≤ 2' for every pair) that does not scale with n_val, so the row's stringency depends on whether the extension happened.
- §5.2 does not say whether F11's L_r,k floors and the N2_q flow null are recomputed on the extended validation set.
- The order of work does not say whether the pre-calibration facts commit follows the extension pull.
proposed_change:
- P8(i): ≤ max(2, ⌈0.10 · n_val⌉) per pair.
- State that after an extension, every F11 quantity (minima, L_r,k, N2_q) is recomputed on the final validation set from real data only, before any model run.
- State that the pre-calibration facts commit is made after the extension pull and its re-check.

section: §0.7 (B1 evidence), §3.2.1 EA-1, §3.2.4 (scaled speeds in J, raw speeds in events), §5.1–5.4 (P2, P3-1, P4-1, P7b, P8), §4.7 (F̂_1), §7 R13(e), §9.1 'B1 measured through one lane'
§5.2 minimum evidence (n_val ≥ 16), §3.2.2 fit-layer validity, §3.5 E1, §5.2 'rough expectation'
proposed_change:
- In §3.2.2, fix the reading. State whether a gap over 15 min invalidates the bins or the lane-day, and state the window (04:00–23:00 for inputs, 05:00–23:00 for scored stations).
- Replace §5.2's expectation with these counts, marked as an estimate from a disclosed read-only inspection.
- Because n_val sits on the threshold, decide now, before the commit, whether the Tuesday/Thursday extension is pulled before calibration as a fixed part of the validation set. The pull is real data only, before any model run, with author approval of the printed request count. Otherwise state plainly that INCONCLUSIVE is the expected outcome.
- State the E14 dependency: if E14 does not switch, Old Shakopee Rd is expected to become flow-unreliable under the step-6 rule. B2's discharge station would then leave the flow terms, although P5a-2 would still use its flow.

section: §5.1 (episodes, C4 window), §5.3 P7a-1, P4-1, §5.4 P7b, §0.7 / D3.4 ('variety at B1 lies in duration'), §7 R13(e)
problem:
B1's measured episode usually ends because B2 activates, not because B1 recovers. Once B2's queue reaches Pioneer Tr, PT falls below 40 mph, so the P_1 condition (PT − AL ≥ 20) can no longer hold. B1 is then hidden, not over.

On my estimate, on 8 of the 13 usable days with both bottlenecks, B1's last episode before B2 ends within 30 min of B2's onset. Examples: 06-07 (B1 to 16:00, B2 from 15:55); 06-21 (15:35 and 15:25); 05-17 (16:25 and 16:30); 08-16, 11-15, 07-12, 05-24.

Consequences:
- P7a-1 (|duration_model − duration_real| ≤ 30 min) on those days mostly measures the error in B2's onset;
- B1's C4 discharge window [onset + 10 min, end] runs into the moment B2's queue arrives at Pioneer Tr;
- the 'duration' that D3.4 and R13(e) name as B1's day-to-day variety is censored on about 60 % of the two-bottleneck days, so the plant gate never tests it there.

The current rows do not reflect any of this.

At the expected counts, the estimability limits leave almost no slack. On my estimate there are 23 usable calibration days, with B2 real-active on 9 and B1 (raw P_1) on 12. Real-active on either bottleneck: 13.
- Rule (iii), at least 8 exact observations per k: B2 may have **at most 1** non-reproducible day out of 9.
- Rule (i), at most 20 % non-reproducible: at most 2 of the 13.
- If B1 is redefined on scaled speeds (issue 1, option b), F̂_1 has about 3 exact observations and is not estimable by construction.

The stochastic PASS is therefore improbable before any fit. The likely route is 'PASS, deterministic-only', and using that plant needs an author decision taken after the plant outcome is known. The over-predictable deterministic plant (round-1 issue 11) could then reach the gate by a choice made after the outcome, which is a forking path.
proposed_change:
- State the expected counts in §4.7.
- Pre-register the deterministic-only consequence now, either (a) no gate run on the deterministic plant, or (b) a fixed substitute spread, for example the Tobit (μ_k, σ_k) fitted per §4.7, re-centred, with P6s and P10 gated on it. The (b) option would be chosen before calibration, not after the outcome.
- Alternatively, set the minimum number of exact observations and the share of non-reproducible days from these expected counts before the commit, as lab conventions, and state the false-'not estimable' risk they imply.
